"""
# SchoolConnect — Single Copilot Instructions Reference

This single document replaces scattered agent notes and is the authoritative reference for AI-assisted edits, tests, and developer guidance.

Overview
- SchoolConnect is a Laravel 12 application (PHP >= 8.2) for managing school structures: subjects, combinations, school classes, students, teachers, and academic rules (grading/division).

Quick Setup
- Install dependencies and run initial setup:

```bash
composer install
composer setup   # project-specific setup script (if present)
npm install
npm run dev      # or npm run build for production
php artisan migrate --seed
php artisan serve --port=8000
```

Where to look (fast):
- Models: `app/Models/` — Student, schoolClass, subject, combination, GradingScale, DivisionScale.
- Controllers: `app/Http/Controllers/` — one controller per major entity (StudentController, SubjectAssignmentController, etc.).
- Migrations: `database/migrations/` — source of truth for DB schema; review timestamps and constraints.
- Routes: `routes/web.php` — HTTP endpoints used by Blade + AJAX.
- Views: `resources/views/` — Blade templates; student listing and modals live in `resources/views/students/`.

Important behaviors (do not change without tests):
- Student registration number is auto-generated in the `Student` model (look for `booted()` or `creating` hook). Avoid manual edits.
- `schoolClass` names and derived fields are generated by model logic (see `schoolClass.php` and the `generateName()` method).
- Level-specific rules: A-Level classes require a `combination_id`; O-Level classes allow `combination_id` to be null.

Database notes
- Primary entity tables: `subjects`, `combinations`, `school_classes`, `students`, `grading_scales`, `division_scales`.
- Pivot tables:
  - `subject_user` — teachers assigned to subjects (contains `subject_id`, `user_id`, `academic_year`).
  - `subject_student` — many-to-many assignments between students and subjects (core + electives). Ensure unique constraints and timestamps are in place.

API & AJAX conventions
- Controllers that support AJAX should return JSON when `expectsJson()` or when requests come via `fetch`/`axios` from the frontend. Keep responses consistent (200 + JSON body on success, 4xx JSON on validation errors).

Conventions and best practices for edits
- Keep edits minimal and surgical. Add unit/feature tests for behavior changes impacting migrations, model boot hooks, or registration generation.
- Use DB transactions for multi-step updates (e.g., syncing subjects).
- Eager load relations where used in lists to avoid N+1 issues (e.g., `Student::with('schoolClass','subjects')`).

Testing
- Run `composer test` or `php artisan test`. Add feature tests for:
  - Student registration number generation.
  - SchoolClass name generation on save.
  - Subject assignment endpoints (attach/detach/sync) returning JSON.

Common troubleshooting steps
- If students have incorrect registration numbers: check `app/Models/Student.php` for the `creating`/`booted` hook and the logic that formats `ARC/...`.
- If subjects do not appear in the UI: check AJAX endpoints in `routes/web.php` and corresponding controller JSON responses; review Blade JS for endpoint URLs and CSRF meta tag.
- If migrations fail: inspect `database/migrations/` in timestamp order; check foreign key dependencies and run `php artisan migrate:status`.

Key files to reference (quick links within repo):
- [app/Models/Student.php](app/Models/Student.php)
- [app/Models/schoolClass.php](app/Models/schoolClass.php)
- [app/Http/Controllers/StudentController.php](app/Http/Controllers/StudentController.php)
- [app/Http/Controllers/SubjectAssignmentController.php](app/Http/Controllers/SubjectAssignmentController.php)
- [database/migrations/](database/migrations/)
- [routes/web.php](routes/web.php)
- [resources/views/students/students.blade.php](resources/views/students/students.blade.php)

If you're the human reviewer
- Run the test suite and exercise the student UI (Details modal, Manage Electives, bulk core assignment). Capture browser console + Network responses for failing flows and add feature tests replicating the bug before fixing.

Contact points
- When updating automation or agent instructions, modify this file only. Keep a short changelog at the top if you need to preserve historical notes.

End of single reference document.
"""
